about: The mutation review (#28, AC4). Each mutant is one exact edit to one file: `find` occurs exactly once in `file`, and `replace` takes its place. With it made, the test `name` in `test` has to fail. `name` is the test's own name, or its suites' names and its own joined by ' > ' where its own isn't unique in the file. `behavior` is the approved test plan's behavior the mutant samples, and `protects` says what breaks. `pending` lists behaviors whose code hasn't landed, with the issue that lands it. scripts/mutants.js runs them, and docs/testing.md says how to add one.

pending.protects: Pasted and imported HTML loses scripts, event handlers, and unsafe URLs before it renders or is stored.
pending.why: No test loads js/sanitize.js yet (#28 slice 1 found it). #21 rewrites the sanitizer with its suite, and that PR adds the mutants.

pending.protects: #20's interim providers report connected or verified only after they verify.
pending.why: The interim providers aren't on next yet. The PR that adds them adds their mutants.

pending.protects: exportAll includes links, custom themes, and note snapshots.
pending.why: exportAll leaves them out today (KD-005), so there is nothing to break yet. The PR that fixes KD-005 adds a mutant per record type.

mutants.protects: A command on the IndexedDB adapter answers only once its transaction fires complete.
mutants.find:
const end = await ended;
      if (end.committed) return answered(first.commit);
mutants.replace:
const end = { committed: true };
      if (end.committed) return answered(first.commit);
mutants.name: a command answers only after its transaction fires complete

mutants.protects: A transaction that aborts after its requests succeeded answers unavailable, never committed.
mutants.find: tx.addEventListener('abort', () => resolve({ committed: false, error: tx.error }));
mutants.name: a transaction that aborts after its requests succeeded answers unavailable, and stores none of them

mutants.protects: Every write transaction on the IndexedDB adapter is opened with durability 'strict'.
mutants.name: every write runs in one readwrite transaction with durability strict, opened in the task that sends it

mutants.protects: A unit that stops its command aborts the transaction, so nothing an earlier unit wrote commits.
mutants.name: a command whose later unit stops it or throws aborts its transaction, so nothing an earlier unit wrote stays

mutants.protects: A failed write doesn't run again once this context sent a later write to the same store, so it can't land over it.
mutants.find: if (overtaken) return { outcome: unavailable('storage', 'transaction-failed', true), replayed: false };
mutants.name: doesn't run a failed write again once this context sent a later one, so it can't land over the later one

mutants.protects: A unit on the legacy adapter answers only once its transaction commits.
mutants.name: a write whose transaction aborts as it commits is unavailable, never committed

mutants.protects: A unit that throws aborts its command's transaction, so nothing an earlier unit wrote commits.
mutants.name: a command whose later unit stops it or throws aborts its transaction, so nothing an earlier unit wrote stays

mutants.protects: A unit declared readonly can't write on the IndexedDB adapter, even in a command whose transaction is readwrite.
mutants.name: a unit declared readonly can't write, even in a command another unit makes readwrite

mutants.protects: The codec refuses a getter or setter, which could give JSON another value than the check saw.
mutants.find: if (!('value' in descriptor)) throw new CodecError('a getter or setter', path);
mutants.name: refuses cycles, symbol keys, getters, hidden properties, holes, and array extras

mutants.protects: The codec refuses an object whose prototype isn't Object.prototype or null.
mutants.find: if (proto !== Object.prototype && proto !== null) throw new CodecError("an object that isn't plain", path);
mutants.name: refuses an object or array that inherits from anything else, which would change what JSON writes

mutants.protects: The codec refuses a property that isn't enumerable, which JSON would drop.
mutants.find: if (!descriptor.enumerable) throw new CodecError('a hidden property', path);
mutants.name: refuses cycles, symbol keys, getters, hidden properties, holes, and array extras

mutants.protects: A save sent with a stale expectedRevision is a conflict, and the newer save stays.
mutants.name: two contexts: when both save one note's blocks from the revision they loaded, the later save is a conflict

mutants.protects: A commandId sent again with another command is rejected as key reuse, and nothing runs.

        const stale = versionConflict(tx, noteId, { expectedRevision });
